subject: Shiny app with googleVis - 2012 best cities of US- some questions

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Shiny app with googleVis - 2012 best cities of US- some questions
parts:
In putting together my first shiny app with googleVis (discussed at http://analyticsandvisualization.blogspot.com/2013/06/revisualizing-best-cities-in-us-in-2012.html), I had three questions regarding googleVis, which Markus Gesmann answered. In that application, I used a motion chart to show scatter plots. Those questions might be of interest to some in this group.They were regarding google chart tools, as Markus explained. I would appreciate any inputs on how these issues can be addressed using alternate tools.  

1. In GeoChart: In my data, I have a variable with a paragraph of  10 lines, say, to describe each country studied. I tried to use that as my hover variable, but there was a truncation of what was shown and it all came in just one line. Is this a limitation of the functionality for now?
Markus: Indeed, I believe this is a current limitation. 

2. In motion chart: example could be the Fruit data in the googleVis package. If we did a basic plot(gvisMotionChart(Fruits, "Fruit", "Year")), the output provides the ability to modify the horizontal axis to sales, profit, expenses, time and the vertical axis provides the ability to Expenses, Profit and Sales. Is it possible to provide only a subset of these vars and not all default vars? For example, could I provide only profit and expenses for horizontal axis, and sales and expenses for vertical axis? Other options being the same (for color, size, etc.)
Markus: No, I am afraid this is not possible. 

3. Can I size a bubble based on a variable such that a lower value indicated bigger size? I was able to create a reordered variable, but two problems it created were (a) the hover value for size was the modified value and not the original value, and (b) this newly created variable was also available as an option for the horizontal and vertical axis, taking us back to question 2 above.
Markus: I don't think so either

Thanks,
Vivek
